decisions: Keep the Lighthouse simulated mobile threshold and throttling unchanged; the repository gate uses simulated LCP, while the LCP breakdown table reports observed trace phases.
Reject and revert temporary content-visibility and font-display optional experiments because they did not produce a repeatable gate pass.
Treat URL-blocked JavaScript and CSS Lighthouse results as diagnostics only; these variants broke runtime or design styling and are not product fixes.

Later D30 all-route Astro static HTML candidate passes G3: all 24 route/profile Lighthouse rows pass, with mobile LCP 1357–1359ms and desktop LCP 327–330ms. This supersedes the earlier Next-rendered fallback failure.
resources_used: Next.js official Server and Client Components documentation: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components
risks: S7 preview deployment awaits owner Vercel authentication; the provisional URL returns 404, so no live production or indexing claim is made.
The Next-rendered fallback retains its historical mobile LCP failure and remains a rollback path; D30 static HTML is the default candidate.
BusinessOS real PR and publish flow, provider receipts, and launch video are not yet verified. Custom domain remains deferred.
open_questions: Owner must complete Vercel device authentication before a temporary preview can be deployed.
next_instructions: After authentication, deploy only the temporary preview and verify routes, headers, contact action, sitemap, robots, metadata and structured data against the actual URL.
Do not deploy production or alter DNS without explicit owner direction. Preserve the prior Next-rendered performance evidence as a historical fallback comparison.
